frequency_question: How often do highly partisan, restrictive federal voter qualification bills pass both chambers of Congress in a single legislative cycle?
membership_rule: Includes standalone bills introduced since 1993 (National Voter Registration Act era) focused strictly on voter eligibility/registration documentation requirements; excludes broad omnibus electoral reform packages like H.R. 1 or S. 1, and excludes routine appropriations riders.

cases.name: The National Voter Registration Act amendments / various proof-of-citizenship standalone bills (e.g., SAFE Act historical iterations)
HR 8281 / Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act (SAVE Act) initial House passage and Senate stall

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 named; believed to be the exhaustive set of dedicated standalone federal proof-of-citizenship bill pushes in this timeframe.
known_gaps: Some early 2000s committee-level markers that never reached a floor vote are omitted as they did not achieve chamber-wide mobilization.
skeleton: Legislative cycles since 1993 where a major restrictive voter ID/citizenship bill was prioritized for standalone floor action, multiplied by the passage rate of such narrow partisan bills in divided or narrow-majority Senates.
multiplier: 15 legislative cycles since 1993 x 2 major standalone push events = 3 total distinct historical legislative push episodes for strict federal proof-of-citizenship bills.
validity_reason: Remains valid through the current congressional alignment and until the next major structural shift in Senate filibuster rules or party control.
